header.title: De Non Conveniendo Cum Haereticis: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Lucifer, Bishop of Cagliari
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's stoa0180a.stoa001.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's CSEL (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. The whole work is translated. It was chosen because no English translation of it could be found.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation of the whole work, checked against the original by a second AI only in samples. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0180a.stoa001.opp-l: 1.1: 'nihil esse debet inter' appears defective (perhaps 'nihil commune'); rendered by sense. 3.1: 'nec si mihi dimidiam domum tuam' lacks a verb, supplied as [you gave]; 'a deo obiurgandum' is probably for 'ad obiurgandum', rendered 'sent by God to rebuke'; 'auerterunt faciem patris sui' follows the Old Latin/Septuagint and is obscure; 'cum audissent qui reduxerant eum de uia, dixit' is grammatically confused in the text and rendered literally. 'sacrarium' rendered 'altar'; 'subiunctorium' rendered 'beast of burden'.

Line 4.1: 'Subrelictorum' renders Paralipomenon, i.e. the books of Chronicles. 'Elieser filius Oziae ex Marea' follows the text given (Hebrew: son of Dodavah of Mareshah). Line 5.1: 'a nobis deo odibilibus' read as 'a uobis' (scanning error); 'conuentioulum' read as 'conuenticulum'. Line 6.1: 'fdle' read as 'felle'; 'donec corrigat dies' is literally 'until the day corrects'.

Line 7.1: 'conprehenderitis omnium errorum' appears to lack a noun (probably 'uiam'); '[the way]' is supplied. Line 9.1: 'eonuentus' read as 'conuentus' and 'cornum' as 'cornu'; 'quam ... ita credentium' seems to lack a word such as 'quisquam'. 'caro tuo diabolo' is taken as 'your dear (carus) devil', which is ironic. 'Edict' presumably refers to an imperial document of Constantius. 'Estote uobiscum' is rendered 'Be with us', since 'with you [yourselves]' makes little sense; the text may be corrupt.

10.1: 'imaui' read as 'iuraui'; 'temperatus' as 'temperatum'. The quotation of Col. 2:18 ('quae uidetur ambulans') is odd Latin; translated as given. 11.1: 'bona gloriatio uestra' stands without the 'non' of the usual text of 1 Cor 5:6; translated as given, though a 'non' may have dropped out. 'scripsi a uobis' makes no sense; read as a corruption of a verb of withdrawing (e.g. 'recessi'/'discessi').

12.1: 'arissimos' read as 'carissimos' (dearest ones, ironic). 'conuiperinis' taken as 'fellow vipers'. 13.1: 'contyranni' = fellow tyrant; 'en)' read as 'ero'; 'am' read as 'aue'; the citation of 1 Maccabees presents Judas as 'the tenth' (decimus), as the text gives it. 14.1: 'temperantes' read as 'obtemperantes'; 'fuissemus eo ueneno' seems to lack a participle (e.g. 'infected'), supplied in brackets; 'principes potestatis aeris huius spiritus' is syntactically loose.

Single long passage. In Jude 1:3 'societati' (fellowship) stands where Jude has 'faith'; translated as given. 'Baal' stands for Balaam and 'Coreb' for Korah (glossary: Korah); rendered as intended. 'adfixmans' read as 'adfirmans'. The Jude 1:6 clause 'in iudicium magni dei uinculis. eos sanctorum angelorum sub tenebras seruauit' seems corrupt ('sanctorum angelorum' does not construe); rendered by sense. 'cinis propositae sunt exemplum' is also awkward and is rendered 'set forth as an example in ashes'. 'tuae interficere laborantes amicitiae' is rendered literally as 'your friendships, which strive to kill'.

nodes.text: I. On Not Coming Together with Heretics.

When you had noticed that all your ruinous attempts had been opposed, and had found all your machinations against the Church of God revealed to the whole people of God, you said that we were, and are, enemies of peace, foes of unity, and adversaries even of brotherly love. If there ought to be nothing in common between the worshippers of God and the enemies of his religion, why did Moses, at the time when he saw that carnal Jewish people, whose wisdom you hold, fall into the guilt of idolatry, after he had had certain of them struck down by the sword, also wish his own station to be set apart? Learn that this is written thus: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to the sons of Israel: You are a stiff-necked people; see that I do not bring another plague upon you and destroy you. Now therefore lay aside the robes of your glory and your ornament, and I will show what I am going to do to you. And the sons of Israel took off their ornament and their robes from Mount Horeb, and Moses took the tabernacle and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and it was called the tabernacle of testimony; and it came about that everyone who sought the Lord went to the tabernacle of testimony, out beyond the camp. And when Moses went out from the tabernacle, all the people stood, each watching at the door of his own tent. They watched Moses going until he entered the tabernacle; and as soon as Moses had entered the tabernacle, the pillar of cloud came down and stood at the door of the tabernacle and spoke to Moses, and all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tabernacle, and the whole people, standing, worshipped, each at the door of his own tent. And the Lord spoke to Moses openly, openly, as someone speaks to his friend. But his attendant, Joshua son of Nun, a young man, did not go out of the tabernacle. By this deed it was shown that you who sin against God are to be shunned, and that we must withdraw from you. But, someone says, see, although Moses had the tabernacle in another place, he still did not desert the people, but urged them to correct the ways of their errors, so that God might be favourable. Nor are those who have refused to be mingled with your sacrilege lacking in these duties; for you know that you are told that unless you correct your ways you will perish for ever.

So then, to carry through to proof, as thoroughly as we can, what we had begun to set out: as often as the people murmured against God and rose up against Moses, you have read that God said to Moses and Aaron: Withdraw from the midst of this undisciplined, obstinate people, and I will destroy them. What then does he want us to do, except to flee you who are undisciplined and obstinate, so that we do not perish together with you, like those who had joined with Korah, Dathan and Abiram? Or will you deny that you are undisciplined and obstinate? Look back at your acts committed against the Church of the Lord, and you will find how undisciplined and obstinate you are. In Deuteronomy Moses says: You shall not make a covenant with them, nor have mercy on them, nor give your daughters to them in marriage, nor shall you give his daughter to your son; for he will lead your son away from me, and he will serve foreign gods, and the Lord will be angry with you in his wrath and will quickly destroy you. Since he commands this to be done, how can we come together with you, have peace with you, with the deniers of the only Son of God? How could we have fulfilled this will of yours? For you see that God said through Moses of the Moabites and Ammonites: You shall not greet them peaceably all the days of your life, for ever. How could Arians and Christians have been together? For you hear Moses saying: There shall be no adulteress among the daughters of Israel; and in every place he warns that every adulterer is to be brought out to the gate and killed with stones: and you shall remove, he says, the wicked one from among yourselves. If he says that God so abhors carnal adultery that he ordered all adulterers to be punished, how much more must the Lord abhor your spiritual adultery; and for this reason you were, and are, to be fled from. We Christians could not come together with apostates, since we find that the Holy Spirit said through Moses: God will open to you his best heavenly treasure, to give rain to your land; in due season he will bless all the work of your hands; you will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow; and you will war against many nations, but they will not overcome you; the Lord your God will make you the head and not the tail, and you will be above and not beneath, if you hear the command of the Lord your God, whatever I command you today to keep and to do, and do not turn aside from any word that I command you today, to the right or to the left. How could we come together with the Arian false bishops of your sect, when you see that we could not have been blessed unless we had not gone after your idolatry, unless we had abhorred your heresy of the Arians, as we abhor that of all heretics, unless we had judged and held you to be such as the heathen are, worshippers, that is, of all demons, unless we had abominated you as we do the Jews, who are found to be without God, since they denied the only Son of God? In Joshua son of Nun it says: And when the people heard the sound of the trumpets, the whole people shouted with a great shout, and all the walls of the city round about fell down, and the whole people went up into the city, each one straight before his adversaries, and they seized the city and laid it under the ban, and whatever was in the city, from man to woman, from young to old, even to calf and to beast of burden, they killed with the edge of the sword. And Joshua said to the two young men who had spied out [the land]: Go into the woman's house and bring her out, and whatever is hers. And the two young men who had spied out the city went into the woman's house and brought out Rahab the harlot, and her father and mother and her brothers, and whatever was hers, and all her kindred, and they led her out beyond the camp of Israel; and the city was burned with fire with everything that was in it. And further on: Joshua kept alive Rahab the harlot and all her father's house, and she has dwelt in Israel to this day. Since, then, you see that all who lived in the city of Jericho were punished with the edge of the sword, and the whole city burned, how did you think we could come together with you, a heretic, when we observed that you and yours deserved the ban more than they had? How could we come together with the Arian false bishops of your sect, when you see that no one was preserved alive in the city in which idolaters dwelt except Rahab alone, because she believed that our Lord was almighty, and that the idolatry in which the people settled in Jericho trusted had been invented by human error?

How could we come together with you, when it is written in the third book of Kingdoms that your houses are not to be trodden, nor food to be taken with you, nor water to be accepted from you? Holy Scripture discloses that this is so: And there came, it says of that fellow apostate of yours, the word of the man of God; and further on: And he stretched out his hand towards the altar, saying: Seize him; and the king's hand, which he stretched out against him, withered, and he could not draw it back to himself; and the altar was split and its fat poured out from the altar, according to what the man of God had said by the word of the Lord. And the king answered and said to the man of God: Entreat the face of the Lord your God, that my hand may be restored to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before. And the king spoke to the man of God and said: Come into the house with me and dine, and I will give you gifts. And the man of God said to the king: Even if [you gave] me half your house, I will not go in with you, nor eat bread, nor drink water in this place, because so the Lord commanded me by his word, saying: You shall not eat bread and you shall not drink water, and you shall not return by the way by which you went. How could we come together with you to worship God, when such heavy punishment fell upon this man of God, who had been sent by God to rebuke King Jeroboam, because he had been deceived by the one who was called a prophet? And he went away, says the Scripture afterwards of that man of God, by another way, and did not return by the way by which he had come to Bethel. And his sons came and told him all the deeds that the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words he had spoken to the king, and they turned their father's face; and their father spoke to them, saying: Which way did he go? And his sons showed him the way by which the man of God who had come from Judah had gone, and he said to his sons: Saddle the ass for me; and they saddled it for him, and he mounted it and went after the man of God, and found him sitting under a holm-oak, and said to him: Are you the man of God who came from Judah? And he said: I am. And he said to him: Come with me and eat bread. And he said: I cannot return with you, nor eat bread, nor drink water in this place, because so the Lord commanded me by his word, saying: You shall not eat bread there and you shall not drink water there, and you shall not return from there by the way by which you went. And he said to him: I too am a prophet as you are, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying: Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water. And he lied to him and brought him back, and he ate bread in his house and drank water. And it came about, as they sat at table, that the word of the Lord came to the false prophet who had brought him back, and he spoke to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying: Thus says the Lord: Because you have provoked the word of the Lord and have not kept the command which the Lord your God commanded you, and have returned and eaten bread and drunk water in this place, of which he spoke to you, saying: You shall not eat bread nor drink water, therefore your body shall not enter the tomb of your fathers. And it came about, after he had eaten bread and drunk water, that they saddled the ass for him, and he turned back and went away; and a lion met him on the way and killed him, and his body was cast in the road, and the ass stood by it, and the lion stood by his body. And men of that city came and spoke in the city where the old prophet lived; and when those who had brought him back from the road heard, he said: This is the man of God who provoked the word of the Lord. And he went and found his body cast in the road, and the ass and the lion standing over his body, and the lion had not eaten his body nor sprung upon the ass. If this was rendered to him because he had eaten bread and taken a drink of water in a profane place among foreign men, what would have been rendered to us if, as you desired, we had joined in friendship with you, whom we know to be a heretic, whom we know to be a denier of the only Son of God; if we had poured out prayer with you Arians; if, finally, we had allowed ourselves to celebrate all that we, priests of the Lord, celebrate together with your Arian false bishops? Meanwhile, recalling your most bitter acts, you ought to recognise that you were sent in to deceive us, as that false prophet was to that man of God; for as he, though a false prophet, said he was a prophet in order to entrap an innocent man, so you too, though you are not a Christian but an Arian, have pretended to be a Christian in order to ensnare us. Then, although the Church of the Lord has always had peace and has cast out you and the heretics of all sects, you said: I want peace to be made firm in my empire, wishing to violate the Lord's peace in us, desiring to split the people of God, working for your heresy, to which you long to make us all cross over. So you lied that you were a man of God when you said that you were making this peace for the sake of our salvation, just as that false prophet did who said: Come back with me, for I too am a prophet of the Lord, and an angel told me. So, I say, you lied when you said that you had undertaken to do this so that you might please God, since you were labouring to join the catholic bishops one by one to the communion of the Arians.

How could Christians come together with you and with your fellow Arians, when you see that God said this to King Jehoshaphat: why had he taken Ahab the idolater into friendship, why had he gone out to war with the enemy of the Lord? For after that Ahab, your partner in sacrilege, had been struck by a deadly wound in battle according to the word of God, and Jehoshaphat, because he had cried out to God with his whole heart, had been restored to his house, holy Scripture says that Jehu son of Hanani, who was a seer, went out before his face and spoke thus: If you help that sinner and are a friend of those who hate the Lord, for this there is wrath upon you from the face of the Lord; but good words have been found in you, because you have taken away the groves from the land and prepared your heart to seek the Lord. If this is said to him, what would be said to us if we had preferred to be friends with you, a heretic and an adversary of God? Or will you dare to say: I am not an enemy of God, as Ahab king of Israel was? How are you not an enemy, when you do the same things that Ahab did? For you attack the religion of God just as he attacked it, and you persecute his house just as he persecuted it. How could it be fitting for us to come together with you and yours, when this king devoted to God was rebuked by God through a prophet because he had joined in friendship with Ahaziah king of Israel? And Jehoshaphat king of Judah, it says, made friendship with Ahaziah king of Israel; he began to act wickedly, and he made him his partner to build ships in which to go to Tarshish. And he built ships at Ezion-geber, and Eliezer son of Oziah of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying: Because you made partnership with Ahaziah, the Lord has broken your work, and your ships have been shattered and will not be able to go to Tarshish. If those things are said to him by the Lord because he had a king of the way of perdition as a partner for building ships, what could be said to us if we, priests of God, held you as a friend, you the destroyer of his house, you the persecutor of the catholic faith? If he broke that man's work because he had been joined to a wicked man, we, I believe, would already have been scattered by a thunderbolt for joining ourselves to you, a blasphemer. How could we, since we are servants of God and you are servants of the devil, come together into one, when God has willed that there be such separation between us and you as between light and darkness, between life and death, between sweet and bitter, as between the holy angels of God who are always magnifying his mercy and those apostates whom you will see tormented with you for ever, unless you snatch yourself away from them? How, I say, could we servants of God be with you, servants of the Antichrist? For it was said by God to King Amaziah in the second book of Chronicles: The army of Israel shall not go with you, for God is not with Israel, all the sons of Ephraim; for if you think you will prevail with these, the Lord will turn you to flight before your enemies, for strength is from the Lord. In what way could we resist the devil if, in so great a crime of yours, we ran with you alongside the enemies of God, with men found without knowledge of God, with those who do not have God, in whom we know there is a troop of demons? For you cannot be deniers of the only Son of God without demons, since none makes you blaspheme except those who have blinded your hearts, so that the truth cannot be grasped by you.

Could we possibly have stayed on your side and consented to your most shameful schemes, when the Holy Spirit says through the glorious David that none are blessed except those who have withdrawn themselves from you, the deniers of the only Son of God, and that only those who have not mingled themselves with your serpentine thoughts will remain blessed? Blessed is he who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, and has not stood in the way of sinners, and has not sat in the chair of pestilence. How could there be a gathering in one place for you and for us, when you likewise hear David say in the sixth psalm: Depart from me, you who work iniquity? If you Arians do not work iniquity, judge for yourself, you leader in the sacrilege of the Arians, who persecute us with dreadful fury because we call ourselves Christians. You should know, then, that we acted rightly in withdrawing from you, who are hateful to God. For how was it fitting for us to remain in your assembly, stained with every crime, and not to flee you, plagues and pestilences? For he says in the person of our people in the twenty-fifth psalm: For your mercy is before my eyes, and I have been well pleased in your truth. I have not sat in the council of vanity, and I will not go in with those who do wicked things; I have hated the church of evildoers, and I will not sit with the ungodly. If your council is not one of vanity, refute me. Is that council not vain in which there is no counsel except that the Son of God be denied, that it be maintained that God the Father is not true Father, that it be asserted that the Holy Spirit the Paraclete is not the true Spirit of God, that the apostolic and evangelical tradition be destroyed, that the tradition of Arius be made firm? In this council nothing else is made firm except what can procure great joy for all heretics and pagans and Jews; all who curse the religion of God rejoice, because they see you, the emperor, carrying out the thing they prayed for, because they observe that you have shown yourself a denier of the only Son of God and a persecutor of his servants. This is the council which you are accustomed to assemble with great effort and all the strength of your empire, precisely so that all the authority of the sacred Scriptures may be dissolved by the authority of your empire, that all truth may be buried, that the lies of your detestable invention may seem true. These are your schemes in that distinguished council assembled by your power. This is why you hate us, because we curse your council of evildoers; this is why we are in exile, why we are put to death in prison, why we alone are denied being seen; for this reason we are shut up in darkness and kept under enormous guard. For this reason no one is allowed to visit us, because, of course, we refused to have any fellowship in your crimes with you, ungodly and sacrilegious men, you concerning whom a prayer was addressed to God in our person, that we should not perish together while living with you, but should be separated from your impious council, from your wicked conspiracy. For he says in the twenty-seventh psalm: Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication when I pray to you, when I lift up my hands to your holy temple; do not drag my soul away together with sinners, and do not destroy me with those who work iniquity, with those who speak peace with their neighbour, but evil things are in their hearts. Give to them according to their works and according to the wickedness of their pursuits; according to the work of their hands render to them; pay back to them their recompense. This is why we are hated by you, Constantius, because we did not want these things to be said of us which are said by the mouth of the prophet about you and yours because of your wicked work, which are said about the Jews, whose imitator you have shown yourself to be. Are you not the emperor Constantius, who pretended to be making peace, when your evil designs were nothing else but that the Son of God be denied, that the apostolic and evangelical faith be destroyed and your Arian heresy built up, that all who did not acquiesce to you be deported, proscribed, tortured in various ways, and finally killed? And for this reason the Holy Spirit, marking out and at the same time striking you and yours, says in the person of our people: Do not destroy me with those who work iniquity, with those who speak peace with their neighbour, but evil things are in their heart. To us you said: I want peace to be made, and in your heart you, remaining an adversary of our religion, were planning to make us idolaters through you; hence you will truly receive according to your work, according to the wickedness of your pursuits, unless you take thought for yourself. We have shunned and are shunning your counsel, which has been made and is being made against God; seeing your schemes even then, the Holy Spirit said by the mouth of David in the thirty-second psalm: The Lord has scattered the counsels of the nations, and he rejects the thoughts of peoples and rejects the counsels of princes. God rejects your counsels brought forward against his Church; for he cannot hate his people, his inheritance, and love you, sons of pestilence, you persecutors of his servants.

You said: Make peace with the Arian bishops of my sect, and be at one; and the Spirit of God says through Solomon in Proverbs: Do not, do not follow the ways of the ungodly, nor envy the way of the wicked; in whatever place they set up their army, do not come there. Turn away from it and change course; for they will not sleep unless they have done evil; sleep has been taken from them, and they do not sleep. For they feed on the food of ungodliness and are drunk with wicked wine. But the ways of the just will shine like light; they go forward and give light until the day sets [all] right. But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble. How could we have fellowship with you Arians, spiritual adulterers? For we keep in mind what is written: Do not give heed to a deceitful woman; for honey drips from the lips of a harlot woman, which for a time fattens your throat, but at last you will find it more bitter than gall and sharper than a sword sharpened on both sides; and the feet of folly lead those who use her down with death to the underworld. But what do you say? That these things were said about adulteries of the flesh? If you maintain that these things were said about adulteries of the flesh, how much more must you spiritual adulterers be fled, so that what is said here may not come upon us through your Arian heresy, a spiritual harlot? For to some it seems sweet to be joined in friendship with you, the king, by taking up your heresy; but they will find it more bitter than gall when they who chose to be with you begin to feel themselves tormented with you for ever in everlasting Gehenna, and then they will say: Woe to us, who preferred the emperor Constantius to God. How could it have been fitting for us and you to come together? For further on Solomon says again: Cast pestilence out of the council, and strife will go out with it; and: Do not imitate evil men nor desire to be with them; for their heart devises falsehoods, and their lips speak sorrows; and: Do not bring the ungodly to the pasture of the just, and do not be led astray by the fullness of the belly. For the just man falls seven times and will rise again, but the ungodly will be weakened in evils.

How can we be with the proud and the transgressors, with you who would rather be found with Judas Iscariot than with the most blessed prophets, apostles and martyrs? For I hear in the hundredth psalm: I walked in the innocence of my heart in the midst of your house. I did not set an evil thing before my eyes; I hated those who commit transgressions; a perverse heart did not cling to me; the malicious who turned aside from me I did not acknowledge; him who secretly slandered his neighbours I pursued; with the proud of eye and insatiable of heart I did not eat. And in the hundred and eighteenth psalm: I have held the wicked in hatred, and I have loved your law. Since you are wicked, being deniers of the only Son of God, and since you must be hated by us, because, abandoning the way of truth, you have taken up [the way] of all errors, because, abandoning the light, you have chosen to go into the outer darkness, how could we have been most dear to you, the abominable head, the destroyer of the house of God, the kindling of all who work iniquity? How [could we have been] intimate friends, as are Valens, Ursacius, Epictetus, Saturninus and the rest? Of whose number, even though they see into what pit they have fallen, they would yet surely choose to perish with you, provided they may enjoy together with you the empty splendour of your reign. How could we have been with you, we who hold in hatred those things which they have chosen to enjoy with you, men who strive to attain those things which will endure for ever? On what account do we and you not agree? Clearly because we have refused to take up your heresy, clearly because we Christians have refused to be made Arians. And who is there, unless he is, as you Arians are, out of his mind, who would forsake the house of God and go to the tomb of the devil?

Now we suffer hatred from you for this reason, that we were and are afraid lest those things be said of us which were said of those deserters, that is, the Jews, whom Jeremiah accuses, saying: Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob and all the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord: What stubbornness did your fathers find in me, that they withdrew far from me and went after empty things, and were deceived, and did not say: Where is God, who freed us from the land of Egypt, who led us out, giving guidance in the desert, in a land untilled and unknown, and in a land without water and without fruit, in a land through which no man passed nor did a son of man dwell there; and he brought you into Carmel, that you might eat its fruit and its good things; and you entered and defiled the land, and made my inheritance a desolation. The priests did not say: Where is the Lord? and the elders of my law did not know me, and the shepherds acted impiously against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and went after useless things. We did not wish to hear these reproaches, and so we said that you and yours must be fled. For the household of God could not come together with you foreigners, since we see that it was said by God to that carnal people, your fellow in faithlessness: Turn your foot from the rough way and your throat from thirst. But she said: I will take courage, for she loved strangers and went after them. Not only, then, did we refuse to go after you strangers, after you foreigners, but we also pronounced anathema on you, sons of pestilence and darkness, lest, if we had withdrawn from the apostolic and evangelical faith and forsaken the way which the most blessed Abraham, Isaac and Jacob held, and Abel, Enoch, Noah, and all the prophets, apostles and martyrs, these things too should have been said by God of us, which were said of your fellow blasphemers the Jews: As a thief is put to shame when he has been caught, so the sons of Israel themselves will be put to shame, and their kings and their princes and their priests and prophets. We refused to be among you, lest that rebuke of the divine voice should also convict us along with the Jews and with you heretics: Why do you speak to me? You have all acted impiously, and you have all sinned against me, says the Lord.

How could we come together with you? For you have read it written in the first book of Maccabees: Then there gathered to them an assembly strong in might from Israel, every one devoted to the law. And all who were fleeing from evils were added to them and became a support to them. And they formed a force, and struck down sinners in their anger and wicked men in their indignation; and the rest fled to the nations to save themselves. And Mattathias and his friends went round and destroyed the altars, and circumcised by force the uncircumcised boys, as many as they found within the borders of Israel, and they pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hands, and they recovered the law from the hands of the nations and of kings, and did not give the horn to the sinner. Could we have been with you, when you see what those who are found to have feared God with their whole heart did to such men? You, a limb already cut off from the body of the blessed Church at the time you became an Arian instead of a Christian, say: Be with us. And the Lord says in the Gospel: But if your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one part of your members perish than that your whole body be cast into Gehenna. And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one part of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna. The Church proclaims that she has cut off Arius and thrown him away according to the Lord's commands, and you say: Take up your fellow plague-bearers and pestilences; you say: Let yourselves perish of the same disease of which I have perished. Sabellius was cut off from the body of the Church just as this Arius, equally detestable with you, has been cut off, whose word has crept like a cancer so powerfully into you that you are now seen to be wholly cancer; nor can you say that you have not been cankered by the word of Arius, since the stench of your cankering has reached every place in your realm, and we all have resolved to shun you, lest we too be cankered by your Arian plague. So, I say, your master Arius was cut off and thrown away, as Sabellius was cut off and cast out, who dared to maintain that Father, Son and Holy Spirit are one person, because he dared to say that he himself is to himself both Father and Son and Holy Spirit; he was cut off because he did not hesitate to say that the Father himself was made flesh in the womb of the virgin and suffered. So Marcion cast himself out, cut off, who refused to confess that the Son of God took up a man from the womb of the virgin and through this was made man. So Paul of Samosata, the master of Photinus, was cut off and cast out of the body of the Church, because he saw fit to say that the Son of God was a man only. So too the heretics of all the sects have been cut off, as Arius was cut off and as you were, who deserved to be cut off because you say of the only Son of God: He was made out of nothing and is not a true Son; there was when he was not. You are all cut off, then, you blasphemers, and cast out by the power of God from the Church of his mercy, because you did not remain in that faith in which the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs remained. You, a man cut off with all your fellow blasphemers from the body of the holy Church, lying in the devil's bilge, dare to say to her: Be such as I am, so that you may be wasted by such a disease as that by which I myself have been consumed. So you supposed that we could come together with you, as though we did not remember that blessed Paul said: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the tradition which they received from us. What reasoning could have brought it about that, deserting the way which leads to the kingdom of heaven, we should take up yours, which hurls headlong into Gehenna? You thought you could ensnare us with the subtlety with which the serpent ensnared Adam and Eve, composing in choice words and most beautiful sentiments an edict in which all the poisons of your heresy are contained. But how could you have achieved this? For blessed Paul has armed us against your poisons and those of your father, saying: This, then, I say, that no one may deceive you with loftiness of words; and again: See that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty seduction according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world and not according to Christ, for in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily. How could we have been seduced by those sacrilegious Arian sentiments of yours, lofty though the words be, when we know that you hold an empty philosophy? How, too, could your speeches be sweet, when we see you holding the tradition of Arius, not of the blessed apostles? To whom he whom you deny to be the true Son of God said: Go and baptize those who believe in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. How should we Christians acquiesce to you, a disciple of Arius, deserting the apostolic tradition, when we find you saying that the Father is not a true Father but is called Father, when you say that he does not have a true Son, but [that the Son] was made out of nothing, when you say that the holy Paraclete Spirit likewise exists out of nothing, while on the contrary we see that the apostles believed in one God the Father almighty, a true Father, a true Father for this reason, that he truly and not supposedly has a Son, and in his only Son Jesus Christ, that is, in the true Son of God, and in the holy Paraclete Spirit, in the true Spirit of God? How could any of those who believe thus have been tripped up by the devil through you, the founder of Arius's blasphemy, when the apostolic faith both confesses a perfect Trinity and acknowledges the single Godhead of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, while the blasphemy of Arius, that is, yours, holds nothing but what has pleased your dear devil, since there is as great a difference between the faith of the blessed Church and your heresy as between light and darkness?

Meanwhile I have rightly said that you are separated from us as darkness is separated from light, because you are sons of darkness, which is why you have also vomited darkness out of your viperous hearts. You hoped to turn us aside from the way of truth, as though we did not know that the Holy Spirit had warned us beforehand through the blessed Paul, saying: Let no one convict you, wishing [to do so] in humility of mind and the worship of angels, who seems to walk without cause, puffed up by the mind of his flesh, and not holding the head, from which the whole body, brought forth through connection and joining, grows into the increase of faith. How could we have followed you, who walk without cause, nourished by the serpent's mouth of Arius, puffed up by the mind of your flesh, made an apostate, when the apostle's precept compelled us to avoid you? For you said that, for the sake of peace, you desired the false bishops of your sect to be joined to us; but how could we have done this, so as to listen not to God but to you, his enemy? We are not senseless, as you are, so as to deny that the Son of God is God, as the Jews deny, sharers in your blindness and leaders of your unbelief, the example of whose rejection the blessed Paul shows when he says to the Hebrews: And Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, speaking in testimony, but Christ as a son in his house, which house we are, if indeed we hold fast the freedom and exultation of hope; for which reason the Holy Spirit says: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, on the day of temptation in the desert, where your fathers tempted [me] in trial; and they saw my works for forty years. And therefore that nation is hateful to me, and I said: They always go astray in heart. But they did not know my ways, as I swore in my wrath: [Never] shall they enter into my rest. See, brothers, lest by chance there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God; but console yourselves daily, while it is called today, lest any of you be hardened in the error of sin. For we have been made partakers of Christ, if indeed we hold the beginning of [our] substance firm to the end. While it is said: Today, if you hear my voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation. For some, having heard this, did not believe; but not all who came out of Egypt through Moses. And with whom was he angered for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose corpses lay in the wilderness? And to whom did he swear that they would not enter into his rest, but to the obstinate? And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief. Let us fear, therefore, lest by chance, the commandment having been abandoned, some of you seem unable to enter into his rest. For it has been announced to us also, just as to them, and the word they heard did not profit them, not being mixed with the faith of the hearers. For we who have believed shall enter into his rest, as he said: As I swore in my wrath: [Never] shall they enter into my rest, although the works were done from the beginning of the world. Yet he said somewhere of the seventh day: And so God rested on the seventh day from all his works. And in this again: [Never] shall they enter into my rest. Therefore, since it remains for the rest to enter into it, and those to whom it was first preached did not enter because of obstinacy, again he fixed another day, today, saying in David after so long a time, as was said before: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts. For if Jesus had given them rest, he would not have spoken of another [day]. Therefore on a later day there remains a rest for the people of God. For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God [did] from his. Who is so foolish that, when he has read these things, when he has received them from the blessed apostle, he would desert the apostolic faith and try to take up heresy? Who will dare to deny him whom he sees to be able to grant eternal rest to those who believe in him, and wish to believe in that one with whom he would begin to be punished for ever? Who is such a man but you, Constantius the emperor, who have forsaken the camp of the Lord and gone over to the house of the devil? We have not chosen to burn, as you have chosen with your lover the devil, but we hasten to enter into perpetual rest. How could we have been caught by your cunning and turned from the way of truth? When the apostle still urges [us] to lay hold of eternal rest, saying: Let us therefore hasten to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall by the same example of obstinacy. For the word of God is living and strong and sharp, sharper than any sword, and piercing even to the division of soul and spirit, and of joints and marrow, and a searcher of the mind and of the thought of the heart, and there is no creature that is not manifest before him; but all things are naked and open to the eyes of him to whom we must give account. Since these things are so, how could any of us have gone over to you, who remain in the faithlessness of the Jews? What reckoning of things could join us Christians to you Arians, when we saw that you were imitators of that nation in every faithlessness? How could those who flee to the house of God emerge from it? [For] in the Acts of the Apostles the most blessed Peter spoke thus, saying: Repent, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For this promise is to you and to your children and to all who are far off, whomever the Lord your God shall call. With many other words also he testified and exhorted them, saying: Rescue yourselves from this crooked generation. Nor will you be able to say that you Arians are not a crooked generation, as the Jews were and are, since you see that the scribes, Pharisees and rulers of the Jews were then called a crooked generation for this reason, that they both denied the Son of God and persecuted all who believed in his divine majesty. You will not, I say, be able to say that you and all the Arians are not a crooked and perverse generation, since you are doing the very things that they did. If they denied the only Son of God, so do you; if they persecuted the servants of his eternal mercy, you persecute [them] too. What then ought we to have done, but withdraw from you sacrilegious men according to the precept of blessed Peter? For on what ground could there be agreement with you? When the Lord has said in the Gospel: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

How could we have been at one? When the blessed apostle, writing to the Corinthians, said: It is actually reported that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not even among the Gentiles, that someone has his father's wife; and you are puffed up, and have not rather mourned, so that he who did this deed might be removed from your midst. If, then, the apostle ordered one who did a deed of this kind to be removed from the midst, evidently so that the whole Church might not be corrupted through fellowship with him, how much more fitting was it that we should flee you blasphemers? If he relates that he handed that man over to Satan, how much more ought you to know that you have already been handed over, from the time when you began to deny the Son of God? I indeed, as absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged, as if present, him who has done this, in the name of the Lord Jesus, you and my spirit being gathered together, with the power of our Lord Jesus, to hand such a man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. Your boasting is good: do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole lump? Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened. Since this is the apostle's rebuke, could Christians be joined to the servants of Antichrist? For how would one not have been corrupted by the poisons of your so great blasphemy, since whoever communicates with you, whether in hypocrisy or in truth, is in enormous danger? Since I have withdrawn from you on account of your heresy, how could we have adhered [to you] again? When there is the voice of the apostle saying: I wrote to you in a letter not to mix with fornicators, not at all [meaning] the fornicators of this world, or the greedy, or robbers, or idolaters; otherwise you would have had to go out of this world. But now I have written to you not to mix [with them], if anyone who is named a brother is a fornicator or greedy or a worshipper of idols or a slanderer or a drunkard or rapacious, not even to take food with such a one. If we are commanded not to take food with you, did you believe that catholics could come together with heretics to celebrate all the solemn rites? Could we, worshippers of God, have been with you who wander astray, with you who have been led through the devil's poison into every drunkenness? How could this have come about, that we, the living, should stand among the dead? When it was more fitting that you, sons of our adversary, should be seen gathered into one, and we, soldiers of Christ, into one against you, so that you might without any doubt be called by all who love God the members and body of a harlot; by which name we too might be called, if we handed ourselves over to you. Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a harlot? Far from it. Or do you not know that he who joins himself to a harlot is one body? For the two, he says, shall be in one flesh. But he who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit; flee fornication. Of what kind do you think the fornication is that we ought to flee? For he who seeks another woman besides his wife is called a fornicator; likewise he who has served idols is said to have committed fornication, since, forsaking God, he has worshipped idols; similarly he who is a heretic is called a fornicator. Learn which of these is the graver crime: to become a heretic, to serve idols, or to commit adultery according to the flesh. Since, then, whether you are Gentiles or heretics, you are called idolaters, each party must be practising idolatry; and since you will understand that those two crimes are vaster than carnal fornication, beyond what can be told, see with what evils you have slaughtered yourself. The most holy apostle still cries out, saying: Every sin that a man commits is outside the body, but he who commits fornication sins against his own body; and: You are not your own; for you were bought with a price. Glorify and carry the Lord in your body. How will you be able to carry God in your body, Constantius, when by rejecting the apostolic faith and taking up the heretical you have declared yourself not to be his whose our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob declared themselves to be, and indeed all the prophets, apostles and martyrs? Then, if the fornicator sins against his own body, how much more do you, who accomplish that work of the serpent not only through the flesh but through the soul itself? Do you not know that he who joins himself to a harlot is one body, but he who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit? We judged that we had to withdraw from you sacrilegious men, lest we too, made [members] in the body of a harlot, should not deserve to be servants of the Lord, but already, like you, servants of the devil. Woe to you, who would not be joined to the Lord, but chose [to be joined] to the devil. And when he says: Do not be led astray; for evil conversations corrupt good morals, what does he command me to do but flee your assembly stained with sacrilege, lest, while I cling to you, I too perish with you?

How could we have been in your malign council? For we find that the blessed apostle said to Timothy: Lay hands hastily on no one, and do not share in other men's sins. Keep yourself chaste. But how would we have been chaste, who by clinging to you would, like you, have been torn away from the chastity of the faith by those dearest ones of yours, the unclean spirits, that is? How would we not have shared in other men's sins, since, if we had judged that we should stay with you, we would have been going to be what you are, that is, members of a harlot? How could we have been Christians with you heretics? For we knew that the apostle likewise wrote to Timothy that we should withdraw ourselves from you heretics: Teach and exhort these things. If anyone teaches otherwise and does not assent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the doctrine which is according to godliness, he is puffed up, knowing nothing, but is sick about questions and quarrels of words, from which are born envies, contentions, blasphemies, suspicions, evil conflicts of men corrupted in mind and bereft of the truth. And so from you, who do not believe as the people of God believes, from you, who do not teach as the apostles of Christ, the only Son of God, taught, from you, who do not assent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ, we chose to live separated; from you, assailant of the doctrine which is according to godliness, from you, puffed up against us through our enemy, from you, who know nothing true but are sick about questions, from you, through whose unspeakable endeavours quarrels of words, deadly contentions and malign conflicts are found to have been born especially in our days, through you, that is, a man corrupted in mind, a falsifier of the truth. We judged that we had to withdraw from you and from your fellow vipers according to the apostle's precept. For he says below: of men corrupted in mind and bereft of the truth, who think that godliness is gain; withdraw from such. On what ground could we have been with you? For in the close of this letter too he urges that you must be fled, you who have fallen from the faith: O Timothy, guard the deposit, avoiding profane novelties of words and the oppositions of knowledge falsely so called, which some, professing it, have fallen away concerning the faith. We had to avoid you, who bring forth profane novelties of words. For we knew that you had brought forth that sacrilegious utterance at the prompting of the devil, that utterance, I say, by which you expressed the poisons of your dogma, saying: There was when he was not, and he was made from nothing, and the power of the Father and of the Son is not one. These things the Holy Spirit did not bring forth through you, but that unclean diabolical [spirit]. How then could we have guarded the deposit according to the apostle's command, if we had stayed with you in your accursed council, when we have resolved to hold to the apostolic faith until the end of death, namely that which we retain as written at Nicaea against your blasphemy and against the execrable endeavours of all your heretics?

How could we Christians have been in your council of Arians? For we have heard in the book of Maccabees that our predecessors, our fellow servants, were separated from those who had made supplication to idols according to the edict of Antiochus, your fellow tyrant: But Judas Maccabeus, who had been the tenth, had withdrawn into the desert and there led his life with his men in the mountains among the wild beasts; they stayed there, eating grass for food, so as not to be partakers of the defilement. You see from this one testimony that we had to withdraw from you, lest we too should have been partakers of the defilement. How should we be joined to you? When the Lord likewise says to the apostles: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees. And to make plain to us that the leaven was unsound doctrine, such as either those Pharisees or Sadducees then, or you heretics of all sects now, bring forth, the scripture follows, saying: Then they reasoned among themselves, saying: Because we have no bread. As they reasoned, Jesus said: Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have no bread? Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves and the five thousand men, and how many baskets you took up, nor the seven loaves and the seven thousand men, and how many hampers you took up? Why do you not understand that I did not speak of bread: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Then they understood that he had not said they should beware of the leaven, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees. Likewise, since the apostle, writing to the Corinthians, deigns to instruct [us] that we must withdraw from you heretics and from all foreigners, how had your heart, in all things fickle and changeable, but in this malignity set fast with mighty strength to the harm of its own salvation, presumed that we could have peace with you or with yours? Do not draw the yoke with unbelievers; for what partnership has righteousness with iniquity? Or what fellowship has light with darkness? And what agreement has Christ with Belial? Or what part has the believer with the unbeliever? And what accord has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God; for it is written: For I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people; therefore go out from their midst and be separated, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean, and I will receive you and will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. How, since your precepts are seen to have arisen against these promises of the Lord, could we believers have stayed with you unbelievers? Could we, running on the way of light, stand with you, men making their journey on a way filled with the darkness of all errors? For who is so foolish that, when he has heard God say: For I will dwell in them, and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people; therefore go out from their midst and be separated, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean, and I will receive you and will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty, who, we have said, is so foolish that he would not wish God to dwell in him, that he would not wish to be counted, once received by God, among those whom he has deigned to call sons, so as not to flee you, made unclean by your heresy? It did not seem right to us that we should have been at one with you, since it is not right for men to stay with serpents either. Or will you deny that those who deny the only Son of God are called serpents in the sacred scriptures? If you cannot deny it, observe that we have acted rightly in fleeing you serpents. You have read the apostle saying to Timothy: Avoid profane novelties of words; for they will advance much toward impiety, and their speech creeps like a cancer. Did you think that men of God could have been with you, whose speech is like a cancer? Likewise, since blessed John commands that you be fled, saying: I rejoiced greatly that I found some of your children walking in the truth, as we received commandment from the Father. I beg you, lady, not as writing you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another; and this is love, that we walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, as you heard from the beginning, that you walk in it, for many deceivers have gone forth into the world who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; these are deceivers and antichrists. Look to them, that you may not lose what you have wrought, but may receive a full reward. Everyone who withdraws and does not abide in the doctrine of Christ does not have God; but he who abides in his doctrine has both the Father and the Son. If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into the house, and do not say hail to him; for he who says hail to him shares in his malign works. How could it have come about that we, soldiers of God, should be with you and yours, soldiers of the antichrist, since the Holy Spirit, giving these precepts through the blessed apostle, did not even permit you to be greeted?

But perhaps you will dare to say: Do I deny that the Son of God came in the flesh, so that I should be called one of the antichrists? You do not indeed, Constantius the emperor, deny that the Son of God came in the flesh, but you say that he whom we confess to have come in the flesh is a creature, you say that he was made from nothing, asserting that he is not the true Son of God. We, on the contrary, who hold the tradition of this blessed apostle, believe [him] the true Son of God; we believe that the Father and this his only Son have one deity. That this is so the Lord shows in his sacred Gospels, saying: He who has seen me has seen the Father too, and: I am in the Father and the Father in me; and: I and the Father are one. We have often said that, since the Father and the Son are two persons and yet he says: I and the Father are one, and: He who has seen me has seen the Father too, and: I am in the Father and the Father in me, he wished us to grasp nothing else than that the eternity of the Father and of the Son is one, their glory one, their power one and their greatness one. For this reason too the apostle says in this second letter: Everyone who withdraws and does not abide in the doctrine of Christ does not have God; but he who abides in his doctrine has both the Father and the Son, so that, gathering from the doctrine of the sacred Gospels, we should believe that God the Father and his only Son have one deity, [and] that he who so believes has God; but whoever withdraws from this doctrine, that is, I and the Father are one — for it is plural, it shows both two persons and one power of these two persons, that is, of the Father and the Son — therefore the apostle says: He who withdraws and does not abide in the doctrine of Christ does not have God; but he who abides in his doctrine has both the Father and the Son, so that we should believe the Son of God when he says: I and the Father are one, namely that the deity of the Father and the Son is one. It is evident, therefore, that you, who do not hold [the faith] as the Lord handed it down to the apostles and the apostles to the bishops, do not have God, because the apostle too, wishing to show the single divinity of the Father and of the Son, said: He who withdraws from his doctrine does not have God; but he who abides in his doctrine has the Father and the Son. You, I say, set without God, you who have neither the Son nor the Father, we know that we have most rightly fled, since it would not have been fitting for us who have God to stay with the enemies of his divine greatness. But learn how hateful you are to God, that we were not even permitted to say hail to you. How could we Christians have been with you Arians? When the apostle Paul says: Avoid foolish questions and genealogies and contentions and disputes about the law; for they are useless and vain. Avoid a heretical man after one reproof, knowing that he is perverse and sins, being condemned by himself. We could not gather with heretics condemned by themselves, lest that voice should strike us too, as it strikes the Galatians of blessed Paul: You were running well; who hindered you from obeying the truth? Knowing you to be enemies of the only Son of God, we fled your wicked counsels, obeying the voice of the apostle who says: Consent to no one; your persuasion is from God who calls you. Do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole lump. We servants of Christ were unwilling to receive you worms of Arius into fellowship, lest we should have been [infected] with that poison of the devil by which you have been consumed. We were unwilling to go with you, that is, with men who are seen to be still outside the knowledge of God, who are still placed under the power of the devil. We the living were unwilling to be joined to the dead, because you are known to be such as we ourselves were before we believed in the only Son of God. That this is so the apostle shows, writing to the Ephesians: And you, when you were dead in your trespasses and sins, in which you once walked according to the prince of the power of this air, the spirit who now works in the sons of unbelief, among whom we all too once lived in the lust of our flesh, doing the wills of the flesh and of the thoughts; and we were by nature sons of wrath, like the rest. Since you are still such as the most holy apostle reports we were before we believed, you certainly had to be avoided, men in whom and through whom the princes of the power of this air, the spirits, work and carry out their every desire; you had to be fled, sons of unbelief, sons by nature of wrath, lest by clinging to you we should be led back to what we had been before. We were unwilling to be with you, because you had not yet obtained the mercy of God which we have now attained. We were unwilling to have fellowship with you, who were led by the counsel of the flesh, as this most blessed Paul was led before he believed, whom we remember saying: Let no one lead you astray with empty words; on account of this the wrath of God comes upon the sons of unbelief. Do not therefore become partakers with them. For you were once darkness, but now [you are] light in the Lord; walk as sons of light; for the fruit of light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth, proving what is acceptable to God, and do not share in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather rebuke [them]. Because we have received these commandments, we were unwilling to stay with you, led by your empty words, lest, that is, wrath should come upon us, as it has also come and is going to come upon you, upon you and yours, upon you sons of unbelief. We were unwilling to be made partakers of darkness, since, now believing in the only Son of God and desiring to obey the commandments of his majesty, we escaped from that darkness and became light in the Lord; hence we did not obey your dark commandments either, because it would have been wicked for sons of light to do your work, the work of a dark man, since the fruit of light is to walk in righteousness and truth and in all goodness.

You say that we act unjustly because we are unwilling to accept your heresy, and because no lasting friendships have been fixed with you and yours. Hear what Moses did concerning the foreigners at the time when God deigned to command him to send a set number of Israelites and destroy with the edge of the sword five kings of Midian and Moab. When those sent to battle had killed all the males, but had spared the female sex that met them, Moses rebuked the sons of Israel for not destroying the female sex as well, and ordered those same women to be killed in his presence, declaring that they could entice the minds of the people to worship idols. If, then, we too abhor your heresy as Moses abhorred idolatry, if we too desire that the heresies of all your erring followers be slain, and by the sword of God, just as Moses [desired] those [women] who were enslaved to idols to be slain, and if we flee you, the adversaries of God's religion, as he fled the worshippers of idols, consider that we act rightly in withdrawing ourselves from you. For how could we have come together with you, when he said to the Philippians: Look out for the dogs, look out for the evil workers? Which of God's servants would not flee you dogs, you evil workers, except one who had forgotten that he was a Christian? Could we, servants of Christ, have been joined to you, adversaries of God's religion, when Jude, the glorious apostle, brother of the apostle James, exhorts us to avoid you and those like you and to remain in the faith we have received until the end of death? Jude, servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to those who are called, beloved in God the Father and kept in Jesus Christ: may mercy and peace and love be multiplied to you. Dearly beloved, while making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I beg you to labour hard for the fellowship once delivered. For certain men have crept in, long ago marked out for this judgement, impious men, who turn the grace of God into licentiousness and deny him who is our Master and Lord, Jesus Christ. It would have been a crime for us to come together with you deniers and blasphemers, when he goes on to set before us the examples of those who transgressed the Lord's commandments and presses our hearts to remain in that faith in which he himself is seen to have remained: I wish therefore to remind you, though you know all things, that God saved his people out of the land of Egypt, but afterwards destroyed those who did not believe; and the angels too who did not keep their rank, but abandoned their dwelling, he has kept under darkness in chains for the judgement of the great God. And Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, since in like manner to these they had committed adultery and gone after the flesh, have been set forth as an example in ashes, undergoing the punishment of eternal fire. In the same way these men too, dreaming, defile the flesh and despise dominion. And below: Woe to them, for they have gone in the way of Cain, and for reward have rushed headlong into the error of Balaam, and have perished in the rebellion of Korah. These are blemishes in your love-feasts, ruling themselves without fear, clouds without water carried about by every wind, autumn trees without fruit, dead, torn up by the roots, wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame, seducing storms, for whom the season of darkness has been kept for ever. And below: But you, brothers, remember the words foretold by the apostles of Jesus Christ, for they said: In the last days there will be mockers, walking according to their own impious desires. These are the ones who cause divisions, natural men, not having the Spirit. Because you, Constantius, have been seen to be in all these evils, your friendships, which strive to kill, have been avoided by us, lest, that is, we should have been hurled headlong with you into those places of torment into which, as [Jude] relates, all those whose path you are holding were cast headlong.
